issue.title: [BugFix] parse_json on deeply nested JSON aborts the BE (no parse depth limit)
issue.body:
### Steps to reproduce the behavior (Required)

The JSON must come from a table column; a constant is folded on the FE and never reaches the BE.

1. `CREATE TABLE t_json_depth (id INT, s VARCHAR(1048576)) PROPERTIES ('replication_num' = '1');`
2. `INSERT INTO t_json_depth SELECT 1, concat(repeat('[', 200000), repeat(']', 200000));`
3. `SELECT parse_json(s) FROM t_json_depth;`

### Expected behavior (Required)

The query fails with a clean parse error, the same as for any other malformed JSON.

### Real behavior (Required)

The BE aborts. A shallow-but-wide document of the same size parses fine, so the trigger is nesting depth, not size. The JSON parsers (velocypack for `parse_json` / `CAST AS JSON`, and simdjson for `format=json` ingest) recurse one frame per nesting level and enforce no depth limit, so a deep document exhausts the thread stack. `CAST(s AS JSON)` and loading into a JSON column are affected the same way.

### StarRocks version (Required)

4.1.4, and present on main. Fixed by #79338 (depends on #79530).

issue.title: Shared-data column-mode partial update publish re-reads every update file once per source segment
issue.body:
### Steps to reproduce the behavior (Required)
1. Shared-data cluster, primary key table with many source segments per tablet, e.g. a staging table loaded in a few thousand small batches (`select count(*) from information_schema.be_tablets` style tablets with 1,000 to 7,000 segments each).
2. Run a column-mode partial update that touches most rows: `SET partial_update_mode = 'column';` followed by a wide `INSERT INTO t (k, c1) SELECT ...` or `UPDATE t SET c1 = ...` that produces several update (`.upt`) files per tablet.
3. Watch the publish on the CN: `grep pcu_update_source_by_upt_us cn.INFO`.

### Expected behavior (Required)
Each update file of the transaction is read from object storage about once per column batch. Publish time grows with the data the update actually touches.

### Real behavior (Required)
`ColumnModePartialUpdateHandler::_update_source_chunk_by_upt` rebuilds the update rowset iterators and reads every update file **in full once per source segment**. Keys are hash distributed, so every update file carries rows of nearly every source segment and the publish performs O(source segments × update files) full reads of the same update data, decoding it only to keep a fraction of a percent each time.

Traces from a production 3.5 shared-data cluster:
- two tablets with one update file and about 800k updated rows each: `pcu_update_source_by_upt_us` is 0.1 s on the tablet with 1 source segment and 18.9 s on the one with 1,213 segments;
- at about 1,213 source segments the time also scales with the update file count: 39.7 s with 1 file, 184 s with 4;
- the largest tablets (7,278 segments × 6 update files, 43,668 full reads) spend 234 s of a 484 s apply here;
- across all CN logs 50,461 s of 93,827 s of column-mode apply time is this re-read.

The slow publish keeps the whole transaction unpublished, so the load appears to hang and following loads to the same tablets queue behind it.

### StarRocks version (Required)
- 3.5.x shared-data; the same code is on main.

issue.title: [Enhancement] Plan a column-subset INSERT as a plain insert when its partitions were never written
issue.body:
## Why I'm doing:

A column-subset INSERT into a primary key table always takes the partial update path when `enable_insert_partial_update` is on (the default). That path writes segments holding only the written columns and, at publish, rewrites every one of them into a full-column segment after looking up the existing rows. For the common case of bulk-loading an empty table in many batches with a column subset, there are no existing rows to preserve, so this is pure overhead: every segment is written twice.

## What I'm doing:

When no transaction has ever committed to any target partition, plan the INSERT as a plain insert that fills the missing columns with their defaults, so the sink writes full-column segments once and publish has nothing to rewrite.

- `InsertPlanner.canPlanAsPlainInsertOnEmptyPartitions`: take the shortcut only when every target physical partition is still at `nextVersion == PARTITION_INIT_VERSION + 1` (never committed to), every missing column is nullable or has a default (no auto increment), the statement is not an OVERWRITE, and the session is not inside an explicit transaction (`ConnectContext.getTxnId() == 0`, where an earlier statement of the same transaction may already have written rows the partition version cannot show). Otherwise the behavior is unchanged. The decision is made per planning attempt and recorded on that attempt's `ExecPlan`, not on the statement, because `planWithRetry` re-plans the same `InsertStmt`.
- The plan-time read of `nextVersion` is an optimistic, lock-free snapshot. `StmtExecutor` records the decision as `InsertTxnCommitAttachment.requireEmptyPartitions`, and `DatabaseTransactionMgr.commitPreparedTransaction` re-checks the partitions the transaction actually wrote to under the commit lock, before versions are assigned. `nextVersion` only advances there, so of two concurrent such INSERTs the first takes the initial version and the second fails with a `TransactionCommitFailedException` asking to retry the statement; the retry sees the advanced version and runs as a partial update. A concurrent regular partial update is unaffected either way. (A follow-up PR makes the FE perform that retry itself.)
- "Never committed to" is read from the partition version rather than row counts because row counts lag publish; a committed-but-unpublished transaction has already advanced `nextVersion`, so it counts as non-empty.
- No new config. Docs: the `enable_insert_partial_update` entry in `System_variable.md` (en/zh/ja).

Tests: `InsertPlanTest.testColumnSubsetInsertOnEmptyPartitionsIsPlainInsert` (never-committed partition is planned as a plain insert; a missing NOT NULL column without a default, an advanced partition version, INSERT OVERWRITE, a missing auto increment column and an explicit transaction all keep the partial update; a re-plan does not inherit an earlier decision) and `GlobalTransactionMgrTest.testPlainInsertOnEmptyPartitionsRejectedOnceAnotherTxnCommitted` (the first flagged commit succeeds and advances the version, the second is rejected, an unflagged commit is unaffected).

Fixes #80745

issue.title: Skip partial update for a column-subset INSERT into partitions that were never written
issue.body:
## Enhancement

A column-subset INSERT into a primary key table (with `enable_insert_partial_update` on, the default) always runs as a partial update. The sink writes segments holding only the written columns, and at publish every one of them is looked up against the primary index and rewritten into a full-column segment.

When the target partitions have never been written to, for example the first bulk load of an empty table done in many batches with a column subset, there are no existing rows to preserve, so this is pure overhead: every segment is written twice and publish time grows with the number of segments.

Proposal: when no transaction has ever committed to any target partition, plan such an INSERT as a plain insert that fills the missing columns with their defaults, so the segments are written once and publish has nothing to rewrite. The assumption must be re-checked under the transaction commit lock, since a concurrent write to the same partitions would otherwise be overwritten by the filled defaults.
